question:
Which of the following idioms given in the alternatives has the meaning?

To reveal a secret or disclose confidential information.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Spill the beans.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "Spill the beans" means to reveal a secret or disclose confidential information, usually unintentionally or before the right time.
◦ (राज़ खोल देना / भेद बता देना)
◦ Example: He spilled the beans about the surprise party before we could decorate the hall.

 

• The idiom is used when information that was meant to be kept private becomes known to others because someone talked carelessly. (गोपनीय बात को समय से पहले बता देना)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Spill the beans.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: Hit the sack (सोने चला जाना): Means to go to bed or go to sleep.
◦ Example: After the long journey, I was so tired that I decided to hit the sack early.

 

• Option 3: Beat around the bush (इधर-उधर की बात करना): Means to avoid coming to the main point and to talk about unimportant things instead.
◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me how much the repair will cost.

 

• Option 4: Call it a day (काम समाप्त करना): Means to stop working on something for the rest of the day.
◦ Example: We have finished the report, so let us call it a day.

question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.

To bite off more than one can chew.
option_1: To take on more work or responsibility than one can handle
option_2: To eat food without chewing properly
option_4: To complete a task very quickly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To take on more work or responsibility than one can handle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The idiom "To bite off more than one can chew" means to attempt a task that is too big or too difficult for one's ability, time or resources. (क्षमता से अधिक काम अपने ऊपर ले लेना)
◦ Example: By agreeing to handle three projects at once, he has clearly bitten off more than he can chew.

 

• The expression comes from the literal image of putting too much food in the mouth at once; in figurative use it always carries the sense of over-commitment, not of eating.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 gives the literal, word-for-word sense of the phrase. An idiom, however, has a figurative meaning which cannot be worked out from the individual words, so this option is incorrect.

 

• Option 3 (To reject an easy opportunity) would be expressed by idioms such as "to look a gift horse in the mouth", not by this one.

 

• Option 4 (To complete a task very quickly) is closer to idioms like "in a jiffy" or "in no time", and is the opposite of the sense of struggling with too much work.

 

• Related idioms of over-commitment: "To have too many irons in the fire" (एक साथ बहुत से काम हाथ में लेना) and "To spread oneself too thin".

question:
Select the option with the correct spelling that can replace the underlined word in the given sentence. If the spelling in the given sentence is already correct, choose Option "No replacement required".

The principal appreciated the student's perseverence despite several failures.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. perseverance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct spelling is "perseverance", which means continued steady effort to achieve something in spite of difficulties, failure or opposition. (दृढ़ता / लगन)
◦ Example: Her perseverance in the face of repeated setbacks finally earned her a place in the civil services.

 

• The word is formed as persevere + ance. The ending is -ance and not -ence, which is exactly where candidates make the mistake.

 

• Correct Sentence: *"The principal appreciated the student's perseverance despite several failures."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "perseverence" — incorrect, because the suffix has been wrongly written as -ence.

 

• Option 2: "perserverance" — incorrect, because an extra "r" has been inserted after "per".

 

• Option 4: "No replacement required" cannot be chosen, since the word in the sentence is misspelt and does need replacement.

 

• Related word: The verb form is "persevere" (डटे रहना) and the adjective is "persevering".

question:
There are four underlined words in the sentence given below. One of them is misspelt. Choose the option with the misspelt word.

The scientist presented an innovative hypothesis after conducting extensive research and collecting sufficient evidance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. evidance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "evidance". The correct spelling is "evidence", which means the available facts or information indicating whether a belief or proposition is true. (प्रमाण / साक्ष्य)
◦ Example: The court acquitted the accused for want of reliable evidence.

 

• The word comes from evident + ence; the ending is -ence, not -ance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "hypothesis" (परिकल्पना) — correctly spelt. It means a proposed explanation made on the basis of limited evidence as a starting point for further investigation. Its plural is "hypotheses".

 

• Option 2: "extensive" (व्यापक) — correctly spelt. It means covering a large area or a great range.

 

• Option 3: "sufficient" (पर्याप्त) — correctly spelt. It means enough or adequate for a particular purpose.

 

• Exam tip: Words ending in -ence that are frequently misspelt include existence, occurrence, persistence, independence and correspondence.

question: Choose the misspelt word from the given options.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Pronounciation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The misspelt word is "Pronounciation". The correct spelling is "Pronunciation", which means the way in which a word is spoken. (उच्चारण)
◦ Example: The teacher corrected my pronunciation of the French word.

 

• Note the important point: although the verb is "pronounce" (with -oun-), the noun drops the "o" and becomes "pronunciation" (with -un-). This spelling change is the basis of the question.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Acquaintance" (जान-पहचान) — correctly spelt. It means a person one knows slightly, or slight knowledge of something.

 

• Option 2: "Embarrassment" (शर्मिंदगी) — correctly spelt. Remember it has double r and double s.

 

• Option 4: "Maintenance" (रखरखाव) — correctly spelt. Note that although the verb is "maintain", the noun is spelt "mainten-ance".

 

• Similar verb–noun spelling changes: explain → explanation, repeat → repetition, curious → curiosity.

question: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to "scarcity".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Abundance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Scarcity" means a state of being in short supply or insufficient for the demand. (कमी / अभाव)

 

• "Abundance" means a very large quantity of something, that is, more than enough. (प्रचुरता / बहुतायत) It is therefore the exact opposite of scarcity.
◦ Example: After the good monsoon there was an abundance of grain in the market.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Deficiency (कमी): A lack or shortage of something; this is a synonym of scarcity, not an antonym.

 

• Option 3: Shortage (कमी): An insufficiency of supply; again a synonym of scarcity.

 

• Option 4: Drought (सूखा): A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall. It is a cause of scarcity of water, not its opposite.

 

• Other synonyms of abundance: plenty, profusion, plethora, affluence. Other synonyms of scarcity: dearth, paucity, scantiness, insufficiency.

question: Choose the word that is the antonym of "Meticulous".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Negligent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Meticulous" means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise in one's work. (अत्यंत सावधान / सूक्ष्मदर्शी)

 

• "Negligent" means failing to take proper care over something; careless. (लापरवाह) It is therefore the antonym of meticulous.
◦ Example: The auditor was found negligent in verifying the accounts.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Careful (सावधान) — a synonym of meticulous.

 

• Option 2: Thorough (पूर्ण / गहन) — done completely and with great attention to detail; again a synonym.

 

• Option 4: Precise (सटीक) — exact and accurate; a synonym of meticulous.

 

• Other antonyms of meticulous: careless, slapdash, sloppy, haphazard, slipshod.

question:
Choose the correct word to complete the sentence.

The committee unanimously decided to ______ the proposal after a lengthy discussion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. accept.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Accept" is a verb meaning to agree to receive or to say yes to something. (स्वीकार करना) A committee agreeing to a proposal after discussion clearly accepts it.
◦ Example: The management accepted the workers' demand for a revised pay scale.

 

• Correct Sentence: *"The committee unanimously decided to accept the proposal after a lengthy discussion."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Except (के अलावा): Usually a preposition meaning 'not including'. Since the blank follows "to" and requires a verb of agreeing, 'except' does not fit.
◦ Example: Everyone except Ravi attended the meeting.

 

• Option 3: Expect (अपेक्षा करना): To regard something as likely to happen. It changes the meaning entirely and is not what a committee 'decides to do' with a proposal in this sense.

 

• Option 4: Excerpt (अंश): A short extract from a book, film or piece of music; it is normally a noun.

 

• Exam tip: Accept/Except and Affect/Effect are the most commonly tested confusable pairs in SSC examinations.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who compiles and edits dictionaries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Lexicographer.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "Lexicographer" is a person who compiles, writes and edits dictionaries. (शब्दकोशकार)
◦ Example: Dr. Samuel Johnson was the lexicographer who produced 'A Dictionary of the English Language' in 1755.

 

• The related noun "lexicography" means the art and practice of dictionary-making, and "lexicon" means the vocabulary of a language or a dictionary.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Philologist (भाषाविज्ञानी): A person who studies the historical development of languages and their literature.

 

• Option 3: Etymologist (व्युत्पत्तिशास्त्री): A person who studies the origin and history of words — where a word came from and how its form and meaning changed.

 

• Option 4: Bibliographer (ग्रंथसूचीकार): A person who prepares lists or catalogues of books and other written material.

 

• Related one-word substitutions: Calligrapher (one who writes beautiful handwriting), Cartographer (one who draws maps), Choreographer (one who composes dance sequences).

question: Choose the most appropriate antonym of the word "Obsolete".
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Contemporary.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Obsolete" means no longer produced or used; out of date. (अप्रचलित / पुराना पड़ चुका)

 

• "Contemporary" means belonging to or occurring in the present; modern and current. (समकालीन / आधुनिक) It is therefore the correct antonym.
◦ Example: The museum has a fine gallery of contemporary Indian art.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Antiquated (पुराने ढंग का) — old-fashioned and no longer suitable; a synonym of obsolete.

 

• Option 2: Outdated (पुराना) — no longer current; again a synonym.

 

• Option 4: Archaic (प्राचीन / अप्रचलित) — very old or old-fashioned, especially of language; also a synonym.

 

• Other antonyms of obsolete: modern, current, up-to-date, fashionable, novel.

question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.

A person who deliberately sets fire to buildings or property.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Arsonist.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An "Arsonist" is a person who criminally and deliberately sets fire to property or buildings. (आगजनी करने वाला) The crime itself is called "arson".
◦ Example: The police arrested an arsonist who had set three warehouses on fire.

 

• The key element in the definition is deliberate burning, which distinguishes arson from accidental fire.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Vandal (तोड़फोड़ करने वाला): A person who deliberately destroys or damages public or private property; the act is called vandalism.

 

• Option 3: Burglar (सेंधमार / चोर): A person who unlawfully enters a building in order to steal; the crime is burglary.

 

• Option 4: Smuggler (तस्कर): A person who moves goods illegally into or out of a country to avoid duty or prohibition.

 

• Related words: Pickpocket (one who steals from pockets), Kidnapper (one who carries off a person unlawfully), Assassin (one who murders an important person for political or religious reasons).

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

No one could have solved this intricate puzzle without your guidance.
option_1: This intricate puzzle could not have been solved without your guidance.
option_2: This intricate puzzle could not solve without your guidance.
option_3: This intricate puzzle has not been solved without your guidance.
option_4: This intricate puzzle could not be solving without your guidance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. This intricate puzzle could not have been solved without your guidance.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is in the Active Voice with the structure Subject (No one) + could have + V3 (solved) + Object (this intricate puzzle).

 

• The passive form of "could have + V3" is "could have been + V3". The object becomes the subject of the passive sentence.

 

• When the active subject is a negative indefinite pronoun such as "no one" or "nobody", the negation is transferred to the passive verb and the agent (by no one) is usually dropped. Hence 'No one could have solved' becomes "could not have been solved". (नकारात्मक कर्ता होने पर वाक्य नकारात्मक रूप में बदल जाता है)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 uses "could not solve", which is still active in form and leaves the sentence meaning that the puzzle itself did the solving.

 

• Option 3 wrongly changes the tense to the present perfect passive ("has not been solved") and drops the modal "could".

 

• Option 4 uses "could not be solving", a continuous form which is not a valid passive construction here.

 

• Rule to remember: Active modal + have + V3 → Passive modal + have been + V3; Active modal + V1 → Passive modal + be + V3.

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Why did the committee reject your proposal?
option_1: Why was your proposal rejected by the committee?
option_2: Why did your proposal rejected by the committee?
option_3: Why has your proposal been rejected by the committee?
option_4: Why was your proposal reject by the committee?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Why was your proposal rejected by the committee?

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense beginning with the question word "Why".

 

• For the Simple Past passive the structure is was/were + V3. Since the object "your proposal" is singular, "was" is used, and the main verb "reject" takes its third form "rejected".

 

• The correct pattern for such questions is: Question word + was/were + object + V3 + by + subject? (प्रश्नवाचक शब्द + was/were + कर्म + V3 + by + कर्ता)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 retains the auxiliary "did", which belongs to the active voice; "did ... rejected" is also grammatically wrong because 'did' must be followed by V1.

 

• Option 3 shifts the tense to the Present Perfect ("has been rejected"), which does not correspond to the Simple Past of the given sentence.

 

• Option 4 uses the base form "reject" after "was" instead of the past participle "rejected".

 

• Related rule: For interrogatives beginning with a helping verb, the passive also begins with a helping verb — *Did he write the letter?* → *Was the letter written by him?*

question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Active Voice?

Let no injustice be tolerated under any circumstances.
option_1: Tolerate no injustice under any circumstances.
option_2: No injustice should tolerated under any circumstances.
option_3: Let us tolerate no injustice under any circumstances.
option_4: No injustice is tolerated under any circumstances.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Tolerate no injustice under any circumstances.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The given sentence is the passive form of an imperative sentence. The passive of an order or command is formed as "Let + object + be + V3".

 

• To convert it back into the Active Voice, the structure "Let ... be + V3" is replaced by the bare verb (V1) placed at the beginning, since an imperative sentence has an understood subject "you". (आदेशवाचक वाक्य में कर्ता 'you' छिपा रहता है)

 

• Therefore "Let no injustice be tolerated" becomes "Tolerate no injustice", which keeps both the imperative force and the negative sense intact.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 is grammatically incorrect: "should tolerated" is wrong, as a modal must be followed by V1 (should tolerate) or by be + V3 in the passive (should be tolerated). It also remains passive.

 

• Option 3 adds "us", converting the command into a suggestion (Let us ...), which changes the sense of the original order.

 

• Option 4 is a passive assertive sentence in the simple present, not an active imperative.

 

• Rule to remember: Active *"Do the work"* → Passive *"Let the work be done"*; Active *"Do not disturb him"* → Passive *"Let him not be disturbed."*

question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error.

Neither of the two candidates/ have submitted/ their original certificates/ for verification.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Option 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The error lies in the use of the plural verb "have submitted".

 

• "Neither", when used as a pronoun with "of", refers to not one and not the other, and is therefore treated as singular. It always takes a singular verb. (Neither of ... के साथ एकवचन क्रिया आती है)

 

• The noun "candidates" immediately before the verb is only the object of the preposition "of"; a verb never agrees with the object of a preposition. Hence "have" must be replaced by "has".

 

• Correct Sentence: *"Neither of the two candidates has submitted his original certificates for verification."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Neither of the two candidates" — correct. "Neither of" is properly used when speaking of exactly two persons or things.

 

• Option 3: "their original certificates" — acceptable in modern usage, though a strictly formal construction would use "his" to agree with the singular 'neither'.

 

• Option 4: "for verification." — correct; the preposition "for" appropriately expresses purpose.

 

• Related rule: Either, Neither, Each, Every, Everyone, Anyone, Nobody, None of are all followed by singular verbs — *Each of the boys was present.*

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The committee was reluctant to interfere ________ the internal affairs of the organisation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. with.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb "interfere" takes different prepositions with different meanings, and here the required sense is that of meddling in someone's matters and thereby obstructing them.

 

• "Interfere with" means to obstruct, hinder or meddle with something, especially with a matter, a process or a person's affairs. (हस्तक्षेप करना / बाधा डालना)
◦ Example: The government should not interfere with the working of an autonomous body.

 

• Correct Sentence: *"The committee was reluctant to interfere with the internal affairs of the organisation."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "interfere in" is used when one takes part in a matter that does not concern one, usually a quarrel or a dispute — *Do not interfere in their family quarrel.* With 'affairs' in the sense of obstructing the organisation's functioning, 'with' is the standard collocation tested in examinations.

 

• Option 2: "into" is not used with interfere; "into" shows movement to the inside of something.

 

• Option 4: "by" indicates the agent or the means, and gives no sense here.

 

• Related preposition collocations: *comply with, deal with, quarrel with, agree with (a person), agree to (a proposal), differ from (a thing), differ with (a person).*

question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options 1, 2 and 3 are not found suitable, choose Option 4: "No improvement required."

The report clearly indicates that the company is capable to achieve its long-term objectives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. capable of achieving.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The adjective "capable" is always followed by the preposition "of", and a preposition must be followed by a gerund (V + ing), never by an infinitive.

 

• Hence the correct structure is "capable of + V-ing", giving "capable of achieving". (capable के बाद 'of' तथा 'V-ing' आता है)
◦ Example: She is capable of handling the entire project on her own.

 

• Correct Sentence: *"The report clearly indicates that the company is capable of achieving its long-term objectives."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "capable for achieving" — wrong preposition; "for" is never used after 'capable'.

 

• Option 3: "capable in achieving" — again an incorrect collocation.

 

• Option 4: "No improvement required" cannot be chosen because "capable to achieve" is grammatically incorrect.

 

• Contrast: The word "able" takes the infinitive — *"The company is able to achieve its objectives."* So, able + to + V1 but capable + of + V-ing.

 

• Similar adjective + preposition pairs: *afraid of, fond of, jealous of, proud of, confident of, desirous of.*

question:
Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

The minister was accused ________ misusing public funds during his tenure.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. of.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The verb "accuse" is always followed by the preposition "of" when the offence is mentioned: the structure is accuse + somebody + of + noun/gerund. (किसी पर आरोप लगाना)
◦ Example: He was accused of forging the signatures on the cheque.

 

• Since a preposition is followed by a gerund, "of misusing" is correct.

 

• Correct Sentence: *"The minister was accused of misusing public funds during his tenure."*

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "for" is used with the verb "blame" and with "punish" — *He was blamed for the delay*; *He was punished for stealing.*

 

• Option 2: "with" is used with "charge" — *He was charged with murder.* This is the most common trap in such questions: accused of but charged with.

 

• Option 4: "by" would introduce the doer of the accusation, not the offence — *He was accused by his own colleagues.*

 

• Related pairs: *suspect of, convict of, acquit of, absolve of, deprive of.*

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The museum had almost emptied by the time the final announcement was made.

A. Realising his mistake, he hurried back towards the ancient sculpture gallery.

B. Only then did he discover that his notebook was missing.

C. The security guard, however, had already locked that section of the building.

D. He thanked the receptionist and walked towards the exit.

S2. He had no option but to return the next morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DBAC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• S1 sets the scene — the museum is emptying after the final announcement, so the visitor is about to leave.

 

• D follows naturally: "He thanked the receptionist and walked towards the exit" — the act of leaving is the immediate response to the closing announcement.

 

• B comes next: "Only then did he discover that his notebook was missing." The phrase "Only then" is a clear time link pointing back to the moment of leaving described in D.

 

• A follows B, because "Realising his mistake, he hurried back" is the reaction to the discovery of the loss.

 

• C comes last: "The security guard, however, had already locked that section" — the contrast marker "however" introduces the obstacle he meets on returning, which directly leads to S2, where he must come back the next morning.

 

• The logical chain is therefore S1 → D → B → A → C → S2, i.e. DBAC.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (DACB) is wrong because he cannot hurry back (A) before he discovers the notebook is missing (B).

 

• Option 3 (BDAC) is wrong because the discovery (B) cannot precede his leaving (D), as B begins with "Only then".

 

• Option 4 (ADBC) is wrong because A (realising his mistake) presupposes a mistake that has not yet been mentioned.

 

• Exam tip: In para-jumble questions, always trace pronouns and link words such as *only then, however, therefore, meanwhile* — they fix the order far more reliably than the content itself.

question:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. The young scientist had spent years working on the experiment.

A. The audience applauded enthusiastically when the results appeared on the screen.

B. After several unsuccessful attempts, the final trial proved successful.

C. She then presented her findings before an international conference.

D. Her perseverance had finally been rewarded.

S2. The achievement marked the beginning of a promising research career.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. DBCA.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• S1 tells us that the scientist had worked for years on the experiment, so the next sentence must comment on the outcome of that long effort.

 

• D follows: "Her perseverance had finally been rewarded" — the word "perseverance" links directly to the years of work mentioned in S1, and the past perfect tense connects the two.

 

• B then explains how it was rewarded: "After several unsuccessful attempts, the final trial proved successful."

 

• C comes next: "She then presented her findings before an international conference." The word "then" shows that the presentation follows the success of the trial.

 

• A comes last among the four: "The audience applauded enthusiastically when the results appeared on the screen" — an audience exists only after the presentation begins, so A must follow C. This leads smoothly to S2.

 

• The logical chain is therefore S1 → D → B → C → A → S2, i.e. DBCA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2 (BCDA) breaks the link, since D (the reward of perseverance) is a general comment that belongs immediately after S1.

 

• Option 3 (BDAC) places A (applause) before C (the presentation), which is illogical.

 

• Option 4 (DCBA) places C (presentation of findings) before B (the successful trial), although there can be no findings to present before the trial succeeds.

 

• Exam tip: Words like "then", "finally", "after" and pronouns referring back to an earlier noun are the strongest clues for fixing the sequence.

question:
Read the following passage carefully and answer the question based on it.

 

Scientific discoveries are often portrayed as sudden flashes of brilliance, but the reality is far more complex. Most breakthroughs are the outcome of years of persistent effort, repeated failures, and gradual refinement of ideas. Every unsuccessful experiment contributes valuable information by eliminating incorrect assumptions and directing researchers toward more promising possibilities. In this sense, failure is not the opposite of success but an indispensable stage in achieving it. Moreover, scientific progress rarely occurs in isolation. Collaboration among researchers from different disciplines frequently leads to innovative solutions that would have been impossible within the boundaries of a single field. However, excessive dependence on established theories can sometimes discourage originality, making it necessary for scientists to challenge accepted beliefs whenever evidence demands it. Thus, genuine scientific advancement requires not only knowledge and technical skill but also intellectual courage, patience, and a willingness to question long-held assumptions.

 

According to the passage, why are unsuccessful experiments considered valuable?
option_1: They prove that scientific theories are always incorrect.
option_2: They eliminate incorrect assumptions and guide future research.
option_3: They reduce the need for collaboration among researchers.
option_4: They discourage scientists from repeating previous work.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. They eliminate incorrect assumptions and guide future research.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The passage states directly that every unsuccessful experiment contributes valuable information by ruling out wrong assumptions and by pointing researchers towards more promising possibilities.

 

• Thus the value of a failed experiment lies in its negative but useful information — it narrows the field of enquiry and shows the direction in which further work should proceed. (असफल प्रयोग गलत धारणाओं को हटाकर आगे की दिशा दिखाते हैं)

 

• Option 2 restates this idea faithfully and is therefore the correct answer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 is an extreme statement. The passage nowhere says that scientific theories are *always* incorrect; it only says that they should be questioned when the evidence demands it.

 

• Option 3 contradicts the passage, which actually praises collaboration across disciplines as a source of innovative solutions.

 

• Option 4 is not supported at all; the passage speaks of repeated failure as part of the process, not as a discouragement from repeating work.

 

• Exam tip: In comprehension questions, options containing absolute words such as always, never, only, all are usually incorrect unless the passage itself uses such wording.

question: Which of the following is known as the 'Universal Solvent'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Water.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Water (H₂O) is called the "Universal Solvent" because it dissolves a greater number of substances than any other liquid. (सार्वत्रिक विलायक)

 

• The reason lies in its polarity. The oxygen atom is highly electronegative and pulls the shared electrons towards itself, giving oxygen a partial negative charge and the two hydrogen atoms a partial positive charge. This makes water a polar molecule with a bent structure and a bond angle of about 104.5°.

 

• Because of this polarity, water molecules surround the ions of an ionic compound, pull them apart and keep them separated — a process called hydration. This is why salts, sugars, acids and many gases dissolve readily in water.

 

• Water follows the principle "like dissolves like": polar solvents dissolve polar and ionic solutes, while non-polar solvents dissolve non-polar solutes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important properties of water: high specific heat capacity (4.186 J/g°C), high latent heat of vaporisation, maximum density at 4°C (anomalous expansion of water), and a neutral pH of 7 at 25°C.

 

• Because ice is less dense than water, it floats — which allows aquatic life to survive in winter.

 

NOTE

 

• Alcohol (Option 1): Ethanol is a good solvent for many organic substances and is partly polar, but it dissolves far fewer substances than water.

 

• Acetone (Option 2): An organic solvent used in nail-polish remover and in laboratories; it dissolves fats, resins and plastics but not ionic salts generally.

 

• Benzene (Option 4): A non-polar aromatic hydrocarbon (C₆H₆) which dissolves only non-polar substances such as fats, oils and rubber; it is immiscible with water.

question: The famous Nasadiya Sukta, which discusses the origin of the universe, is found in which Veda?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rigveda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Nasadiya Sukta, also known as the Hymn of Creation, is the 129th hymn of the 10th Mandala of the Rigveda. (सृष्टि सूक्त — ऋग्वेद के दसवें मंडल में)

 

• It is celebrated for its philosophical and sceptical tone: it questions how the universe came into being, and concludes that perhaps even the highest seer in the highest heaven may not know the answer. It is regarded as one of the earliest expressions of philosophical doubt in world literature.

 

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and the oldest text in any Indo-European language. It contains 1,028 hymns (suktas) arranged in 10 mandalas, composed in praise of deities such as Indra, Agni, Varuna and Soma.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other famous hymns of the Rigveda: the Purusha Sukta (10th Mandala), which mentions the four varnas for the first time; the Gayatri Mantra (3rd Mandala), addressed to Savitri; and the Nadi Sukta, which lists the rivers of the Rigvedic period.

 

• Mandalas II to VII are the oldest and are called the family books (Gotra mandalas); Mandalas I and X are the latest additions.

 

• India's national motto "Satyameva Jayate" is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad of the Atharvaveda.

 

NOTE

 

• Samaveda (Option 2): The book of chants, largely borrowed from the Rigveda and set to music; it is regarded as the origin of Indian classical music.

 

• Yajurveda (Option 3): The book of sacrificial formulae and rituals; it has two branches, Shukla (White) and Krishna (Black) Yajurveda, and is written in both prose and verse.

 

• Atharvaveda (Option 4): The book of magical charms, spells and remedies, dealing with everyday life, medicine and popular beliefs; it is the last of the four Vedas.

question: Which Delhi Sultan introduced the system of branding horses (Dagh) and maintaining descriptive rolls (Chehra) for soldiers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alauddin Khalji.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Alauddin Khalji (1296-1316) of the Khalji dynasty introduced the systems of Dagh (branding of horses) and Chehra (descriptive roll of soldiers). (घोड़ों को दागना तथा सैनिकों का हुलिया लिखना)

 

• The purpose was to end corruption in the army: Dagh prevented soldiers from presenting inferior or borrowed horses at the muster, while Chehra recorded the physical description of each soldier so that no substitute could take his place.

 

• Alauddin was the first Sultan to maintain a large standing army paid in cash directly from the royal treasury, instead of assigning iqtas for military service.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Alauddin Khalji's market (price) control measures are equally important for examinations. He established four separate markets in Delhi — the Mandi (grain), the Sarai Adl (cloth and manufactured goods), the market for horses, slaves and cattle, and the general market. Officers included the Shahna-i-Mandi (market controller), Diwan-i-Riyasat and Munhiyan (spies/reporters).

 

• He raised land revenue to 50% of the produce (Kharaj), imposed Ghari (house tax) and Charai (grazing tax), and measured land (Masahat) for assessment.

 

• He repulsed repeated Mongol invasions, built the Alai Darwaza and Siri Fort, and his southern campaigns were led by Malik Kafur. Amir Khusrau was the famous poet of his court.

 

NOTE

 

• Iltutmish (Option 1): The real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate; he introduced the silver Tanka and copper Jital, organised the Iqta system and formed the Turkan-i-Chihalgani (Corps of Forty).

 

• Muhammad bin Tughlaq (Option 3): Known for the transfer of the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad and the introduction of token currency of bronze and copper.

 

• Firoz Shah Tughlaq (Option 4): Known for building canals, founding cities such as Firozabad, Hisar and Jaunpur, establishing the Diwan-i-Khairat and Diwan-i-Bandagan, and imposing Jizya on Brahmins.

question: Which Five-Year Plan is popularly known as the 'Gadgil Plan'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fourth Five-Year Plan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74) is popularly known as the Gadgil Plan, after D. R. Gadgil, the then Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission, who was its chief architect. (गाडगिल योजना)

 

• Its twin objectives were "Growth with Stability" and "Progressive achievement of Self-reliance". It was launched after the three-year Plan Holiday (1966-69), which followed the wars of 1962 and 1965 and the severe droughts of the mid-1960s.

 

• Major events of this plan period include the nationalisation of 14 major banks in 1969, the launching of the Green Revolution on a wider scale, the 1971 Indo-Pak war and the refugee crisis, and India's first nuclear test at Pokhran in 1974.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gadgil Formula, also named after D. R. Gadgil, was adopted in 1969 for the distribution of central assistance to the states; it was later modified as the Gadgil-Mukherjee Formula (1991), which gave 60% weightage to population.

 

• Quick revision of plan nicknames: First Plan — based on the Harrod-Domar model; Second Plan (1956-61) — the Mahalanobis model / Nehru-Mahalanobis Plan, focused on heavy industry; Fifth Plan (1974-79) — Garibi Hatao, based on the D. P. Dhar model; Sixth Plan — removal of poverty and technological self-reliance; Seventh Plan — Food, Work and Productivity.

 

NOTE

 

• Second Five-Year Plan (Option 1): Also called the Mahalanobis Plan; it laid the foundation of public sector heavy industries such as the steel plants at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela.

 

• Third Five-Year Plan (Option 2): Aimed at making the economy self-reliant and self-generating, but failed because of the Chinese aggression (1962), the Indo-Pak war (1965) and severe drought.

 

• Fifth Five-Year Plan (Option 4): Focused on poverty removal and self-reliance; it was terminated one year early in 1978 by the Janata Government, which introduced the Rolling Plan.

question: Which philosopher propounded the philosophy of Dvaita (Dualism)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhvacharya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhvacharya (1238-1317 CE) propounded the philosophy of Dvaita, that is, Dualism. (द्वैतवाद)

 

• According to Dvaita, Brahman (God, identified with Vishnu) and the individual soul (Jiva) are two eternally distinct realities. The soul is dependent on God but never becomes identical with Him, and the world is real, not an illusion.

 

• Madhvacharya was born in Pajaka near Udupi in Karnataka and founded the Brahma Sampradaya. His school is also known as Tattvavada. Salvation, according to him, comes through devotion (bhakti) and the grace of Vishnu.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major schools of Vedanta frequently asked in SSC:
◦ Adi Shankaracharya — Advaita (Non-dualism): Brahman alone is real, the world is Maya, and the soul is identical with Brahman.
◦ Ramanujacharya — Vishishtadvaita (Qualified Non-dualism): Brahman is qualified by souls and matter, which form His body.
◦ Madhvacharya — Dvaita (Dualism).
◦ Nimbarkacharya — Dvaitadvaita (Dualistic Non-dualism / Bhedabheda).
◦ Vallabhacharya — Shuddhadvaita (Pure Non-dualism), Pushtimarga.

 

NOTE

 

• Ramanuja (Option 1): An 11th-12th century philosopher from Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu, who propounded Vishishtadvaita and founded the Sri Sampradaya.

 

• Vallabhacharya (Option 3): Propounded Shuddhadvaita and founded the Pushtimarga, centred on the worship of Krishna as Shrinathji.

 

• Nimbarkacharya (Option 4): Propounded Dvaitadvaita, which holds that the soul and God are both different and non-different; he was a devotee of Radha-Krishna.

question: Which layer of the Earth's atmosphere contains the ozone layer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stratosphere.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The ozone layer (ozonosphere) lies in the Stratosphere, at a height of roughly 15 to 35 km above the Earth's surface. (समताप मंडल में ओज़ोन परत)

 

• The stratosphere extends from about 12 km to 50 km. In it, temperature increases with height, because ozone absorbs the sun's ultraviolet (UV) radiation and heats the layer. This makes the stratosphere very stable, free of clouds and turbulence — which is why jet aircraft prefer to fly in its lower part.

 

• Ozone (O₃) shields life on Earth by absorbing harmful UV-B rays, which would otherwise cause skin cancer, cataracts and damage to crops. Ozone is therefore called the protective umbrella of the Earth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ozone depletion is caused mainly by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). The Montreal Protocol (1987) was adopted to phase out ozone-depleting substances, and 16 September is observed as the World Ozone Day. The ozone hole is largest over Antarctica.

 

• Layers of the atmosphere in order: Troposphere → Stratosphere → Mesosphere → Thermosphere → Exosphere.

 

NOTE

 

• Troposphere (Option 1): The lowest layer, about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator. All weather phenomena — clouds, rain, storms — occur here; temperature falls with height at about 6.5°C per km (normal lapse rate).

 

• Mesosphere (Option 3): Extends from about 50 km to 80 km. Temperature falls with height and reaches about -100°C at the mesopause, the coldest part of the atmosphere. Meteors burn up in this layer.

 

• Thermosphere (Option 4): Lies above the mesosphere; temperature rises sharply with height. It contains the ionosphere, which reflects radio waves back to Earth and is the seat of the aurora.

question: Which ruler of Magadha founded the Haryanka Dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bimbisara.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bimbisara (c. 544-492 BCE) was the founder and the first important ruler of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha, with its capital at Rajgir (Girivraja). (हर्यक वंश के संस्थापक)

 

• He followed a policy of matrimonial alliances to strengthen Magadha: he married Kosaladevi (sister of Prasenajit of Kosala, who brought Kashi as dowry), Chellana of Vaishali (Lichchhavi) and Khema of Madra (Punjab).

 

• He annexed Anga by defeating its ruler Brahmadatta, giving Magadha control over the trade route to the eastern ports. He was a contemporary and patron of both Gautama Buddha and Mahavira, and the royal physician Jivaka served his court.

 

• He was imprisoned and killed by his own son Ajatashatru.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Dynasties of Magadha in order: Haryanka → Shishunaga → Nanda → Maurya → Shunga → Kanva.

 

• The rise of Magadha was helped by its fertile alluvial soil, the iron ore deposits of the Chhotanagpur region, the location of Rajgir among five hills and of Pataliputra at the confluence of rivers, and the use of elephants in war.

 

NOTE

 

• Ajatashatru (Option 1): Son and successor of Bimbisara; he defeated the Lichchhavis of Vaishali using the Rathamusala (scythed chariot) and Mahashilakantaka (stone-throwing engine), and convened the First Buddhist Council at Rajgir.

 

• Mahapadma Nanda (Option 3): Founder of the Nanda dynasty, described as Ekarat and Sarvakshatrantaka (destroyer of all Kshatriyas); the last Nanda ruler was Dhana Nanda.

 

• Chandragupta Maurya (Option 4): Overthrew the Nandas around 322-321 BCE with the help of Chanakya and founded the Mauryan Empire.

question: Which of the following folk dances is associated with the state of Rajasthan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kalbelia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalbelia is a famous folk dance of Rajasthan, performed by the women of the Kalbelia (snake-charmer) community. (कालबेलिया — राजस्थान)

 

• The dancers wear a long, black, flowing skirt called an angrakhi with a odhani and choli, and their swirling movements imitate the motion of a serpent. The accompanying instruments are the been (pungi), dholak and khanjari.

 

• The Kalbelia folk songs and dances of Rajasthan were inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other folk dances of Rajasthan: Ghoomar (the state's best-known dance, performed by Bhil women), Kachhi Ghodi, Chari, Terah Taali, Bhavai, Gair and Kathputli (puppetry).

 

• India's UNESCO intangible heritage entries also include Kutiyattam, Vedic chanting, Ramlila, Ramman, Chhau dance, Buddhist chanting of Ladakh, Sankirtana of Manipur, Yoga, Kumbh Mela, Durga Puja of Kolkata and Garba of Gujarat.

 

NOTE

 

• Rouf (Option 1): A graceful folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir, performed by women especially during Ramzan and spring.

 

• Bihu (Option 3): The most famous folk dance of Assam, associated with the Bihu festival that marks the Assamese New Year and the harvest.

 

• Lavani (Option 4): A vigorous and popular folk dance of Maharashtra, traditionally performed to the beat of the dholki; Tamasha is the related theatre form.

question: Which part of the human brain is responsible for maintaining body balance and posture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cerebellum.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cerebellum, situated below the cerebrum at the back of the skull, is responsible for maintaining body balance, posture and equilibrium, and for coordinating voluntary muscular movements. (अनुमस्तिष्क — शरीर का संतुलन)

 

• It makes precise, smooth movements possible — walking in a straight line, riding a bicycle, threading a needle or picking up a pencil. It is part of the hindbrain, along with the pons and the medulla oblongata.

 

• Damage to the cerebellum causes loss of balance, an unsteady gait and jerky, uncoordinated movements (ataxia). Alcohol impairs the cerebellum, which is why an intoxicated person staggers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The human brain has three main parts — the forebrain (cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus), the midbrain, and the hindbrain (cerebellum, pons, medulla oblongata).

 

• The brain is protected by the cranium (skull) and three membranes called the meninges, and is cushioned by cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). The average adult human brain weighs about 1.36 kg.

 

NOTE

 

• Cerebrum (Option 1): The largest part of the brain and the seat of intelligence, memory, thought, speech, will power and voluntary action. It is divided into two hemispheres and four lobes — frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital.

 

• Medulla Oblongata (Option 2): Controls involuntary actions such as heartbeat, breathing, blood pressure, swallowing, coughing, sneezing and vomiting. It connects the brain to the spinal cord.

 

• Hypothalamus (Option 4): Regulates body temperature, hunger, thirst, sleep and emotions, and controls the pituitary gland, which is called the master gland of the body.

question: Hemis Festival is celebrated in which Union Territory of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ladakh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Hemis Festival is celebrated in the Union Territory of Ladakh, at the Hemis Monastery (Gompa) situated about 45 km from Leh. (हेमिस उत्सव — लद्दाख)

 

• It is held annually on the 10th day of the Tibetan lunar month, usually in June or July, to commemorate the birth anniversary of Guru Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), who is credited with spreading Buddhism in Tibet.

 

• The chief attraction is the masked dance called the Chham dance, performed by the lamas in colourful robes and masks, symbolising the victory of good over evil. Once every twelve years, in the Year of the Monkey, the giant thangka of Guru Padmasambhava is unveiled.

 

• Hemis Monastery belongs to the Drukpa lineage of Tibetan Buddhism and was re-established in 1672 under King Sengge Namgyal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other festivals of Ladakh: Losar (Tibetan New Year), Ladakh Harvest Festival, Sindhu Darshan, Yuru Kabgyat, Dosmoche and Galdan Namchot.

 

• Ladakh became a separate Union Territory without a legislature on 31 October 2019, following the reorganisation of the state of Jammu & Kashmir. Leh and Kargil are its two districts, and Hemis National Park is famous for the snow leopard.

 

NOTE

 

• Jammu & Kashmir (Option 1): Its well-known festivals include Tulip Festival (Srinagar), Baisakhi, Shikara Festival and Navreh.

 

• Chandigarh (Option 3): Known for the Rose Festival held at the Zakir Hussain Rose Garden and the Chandigarh Carnival.

 

• Delhi (Option 4): Known for the Qutub Festival, Delhi International Arts Festival and Phool Walon Ki Sair.

question: Which lake is known as the 'Floating Lake' of India due to the presence of floating vegetation called Phumdis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Loktak Lake.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Loktak Lake, situated in Manipur near Moirang, is known as the "Floating Lake" because of the floating masses of vegetation, soil and organic matter called Phumdis. (लोकटक झील — मणिपुर)

 

• It is the largest freshwater lake in North-East India and is the site of the world's only floating national park, the Keibul Lamjao National Park, which is the last natural habitat of the endangered Sangai — the brow-antlered deer, also called the dancing deer of Manipur.

 

• Loktak was designated a Ramsar site in 1990 and was later placed on the Montreux Record in 1993 on account of ecological degradation. It also supports the Loktak Hydroelectric Project.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Local fishermen live on the phumdis in huts called phumsangs and practise fishing within circular enclosures known as athaphums.

 

• Other important lakes for SSC: Chilika (Odisha) — largest brackish-water lagoon in India; Vembanad (Kerala) — longest lake in India; Sambhar (Rajasthan) — largest inland saltwater lake; Kolleru (Andhra Pradesh); Sasthamkotta (Kerala) — largest freshwater lake of Kerala.

 

NOTE

 

• Dal Lake (Option 1): In Srinagar, Jammu & Kashmir; famous for its houseboats (shikaras) and floating gardens, and often called the "Jewel in the crown of Kashmir".

 

• Wular Lake (Option 2): Also in Jammu & Kashmir; the largest freshwater lake in India, of tectonic origin, fed by the Jhelum river.

 

• Pulicat Lake (Option 4): The second largest brackish-water lagoon in India, lying on the border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu; the Sriharikota island and the Satish Dhawan Space Centre lie on its seaward side.

question: In which year was the first synchronous Census conducted throughout British India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1881.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first synchronous (simultaneous) census covering the whole of British India was conducted in 1881 under Lord Ripon, and it was supervised by W. C. Plowden, the Census Commissioner of India. (1881 — पहली समकालिक जनगणना)

 

• 'Synchronous' means that the enumeration was carried out on the same reference date throughout the country, which made the data comparable and reliable for the first time.

 

• Since 1881, the census has been held regularly every ten years (decennially), and 1881 is therefore regarded as the beginning of the modern census system in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first non-synchronous census in India was conducted between 1865 and 1872 under Lord Mayo, and is usually referred to as the census of 1872.

 

• The Indian census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs, and is governed by the Census Act, 1948.

 

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th after independence. Its slogan was "Our Census, Our Future". It recorded a population of about 121.09 crore, a sex ratio of 943, a literacy rate of 74.04%, and a density of 382 persons per sq km. Uttar Pradesh was the most populous state and Kerala had the highest literacy and the highest sex ratio (1084).

 

NOTE

 

• 1872 (Option 1): The first census attempt, but it was not synchronous — different provinces were enumerated at different times.

 

• 1891 (Option 3) and 1901 (Option 4): These were later decennial censuses conducted after the system had already been regularised in 1881.

question: Which space agency launched the first module of the International Space Station (ISS)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Roscosmos.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The first module of the International Space Station (ISS), named Zarya (meaning "Dawn"), was launched by Russia through its space agency Roscosmos on 20 November 1998 from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, using a Proton rocket. (ISS का पहला मॉड्यूल — ज़ार्या)

 

• Zarya, also called the Functional Cargo Block (FGB), provided the early station with electrical power, storage, propulsion and guidance.

 

• Two weeks later, on 4 December 1998, the American module Unity (Node 1) was carried up by the Space Shuttle Endeavour and joined to Zarya, beginning the assembly of the station in orbit.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ISS is a joint project of five space agencies — NASA (USA), Roscosmos (Russia), JAXA (Japan), ESA (Europe) and CSA (Canada).

 

• It orbits at an altitude of roughly 400 km in Low Earth Orbit, and has been continuously occupied since November 2000. It is the largest artificial object in space.

 

• In 2025, Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla became the first Indian to visit the ISS, as part of the Axiom-4 mission. Rakesh Sharma remains the first Indian in space (1984, aboard the Soviet Soyuz T-11).

 

NOTE

 

• ISRO (Option 1): The Indian Space Research Organisation, founded in 1969, headquartered at Bengaluru; it is not a partner in the ISS but is developing its own Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS).

 

• NASA (Option 2): The US agency, established in 1958; it launched the Unity module, the second module of the ISS.

 

• ESA (Option 4): The European Space Agency, headquartered in Paris; it contributed the Columbus laboratory module.

question: Approximately how much time does the International Space Station take to complete one revolution around the Earth?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 90 minutes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Space Station (ISS) completes one revolution around the Earth in approximately 90 minutes (about 92-93 minutes). (लगभग 90 मिनट में एक परिक्रमा)

 

• It travels at an orbital speed of roughly 28,000 km per hour (about 7.66 km per second) at an altitude of about 400 km in Low Earth Orbit.

 

• Because of this, the ISS goes around the Earth about 16 times a day, and the crew on board experiences roughly 16 sunrises and 16 sunsets in every 24 hours.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ISS is inclined at about 51.6° to the equator, which allows it to pass over most of the inhabited parts of the Earth and to be reached from launch sites in both Russia and the USA.

 

• Objects in orbit experience microgravity, often loosely called weightlessness. This is not because gravity is absent, but because the station and everything in it are in a state of continuous free fall around the Earth.

 

• The lower the orbit, the shorter the period: a satellite in geostationary orbit at about 35,786 km takes 24 hours, matching the Earth's rotation, and therefore appears fixed over one point on the equator.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (60, 75 and 120 minutes): No orbit at the ISS's altitude corresponds to these periods. By Kepler's third law, the orbital period depends on the radius of the orbit; a period of 120 minutes would require a considerably higher orbit, and 60 minutes would require an orbit inside the Earth's atmosphere, which is not physically possible.

question: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman of which of the following committees of the Constituent Assembly?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Drafting Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dr. B. R. Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly, which was set up on 29 August 1947. (प्रारूप समिति के अध्यक्ष)

 

• The Drafting Committee had seven members: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar (Chairman), N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, Dr. K. M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (who replaced B. L. Mitter) and T. T. Krishnamachari (who replaced D. P. Khaitan after his death).

 

• The committee was entrusted with preparing the draft of the new Constitution, and for this work Dr. Ambedkar is honoured as the "Father of the Indian Constitution" and the Chief Architect of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Important committees of the Constituent Assembly and their chairmen:
◦ Union Powers Committee — Jawaharlal Nehru
◦ Union Constitution Committee — Jawaharlal Nehru
◦ Provincial Constitution Committee — Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
◦ Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights and Minorities — Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
◦ Steering Committee — Dr. Rajendra Prasad
◦ Rules of Procedure Committee — Dr. Rajendra Prasad
◦ States Committee — Jawaharlal Nehru
◦ Flag Committee — J. B. Kripalani

 

• The Constituent Assembly was constituted in 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan. Its first meeting was held on 9 December 1946, with Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha as temporary Chairman; Dr. Rajendra Prasad was later elected its permanent President. B. N. Rau was the Constitutional Adviser.

 

• The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950. It took 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to prepare.

 

NOTE

 

• Union Powers Committee (Option 1) and Steering Committee (Option 2) were chaired by Jawaharlal Nehru and Dr. Rajendra Prasad respectively.

 

• Advisory Committee (Option 4) on Fundamental Rights, Minorities and Tribal and Excluded Areas was chaired by Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.

question: Which organisation developed the indigenous 'Bhargavastra' counter-drone system?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhargavastra is an indigenously developed low-cost counter-drone system designed by Solar Defence and Aerospace Limited (SDAL), a private Indian defence firm. (स्वदेशी एंटी-ड्रोन प्रणाली)

 

• It is a hard-kill counter-swarm system, meaning it is meant to physically destroy swarms of drones rather than merely jam them. It uses micro-rockets and micro-missiles in a layered arrangement to neutralise multiple incoming unmanned aerial systems.

 

• The system is designed to detect small aerial targets at a range of several kilometres and to engage them in salvo mode, making it suitable for protecting high-value installations against low-cost drone attacks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other counter-drone efforts include the DRDO Anti-Drone System (D-4), which combines soft kill (jamming and spoofing) with hard kill (laser) options, and the indigenous air defence systems Akash, QRSAM and the MR-SAM developed jointly with Israel.

 

• Drone-related terms often asked in examinations: UAV (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle), swarm drones, and the regulatory framework of the Drone Rules, 2021 issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

 

NOTE

 

• Bharat Dynamics Limited (Option 1): A defence PSU based at Hyderabad, which manufactures missiles such as Akash, Konkurs, Milan and Astra.

 

• Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (Option 3): A defence PSU headquartered at Bengaluru, which builds aircraft and helicopters such as the Tejas (LCA), Dhruv, Prachand (LCH) and Rudra.

 

• DRDO (Option 4): Established in 1958 with headquarters at New Delhi; it is the premier defence research body of India, but Bhargavastra was developed by a private firm, not by DRDO.

question: In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium vibrate:
option_1: Perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation
option_2: Parallel to the direction of wave propagation
option_3: In a circular path around the source
solution_text:
The correct answer is Parallel to the direction of wave propagation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth along the same direction in which the wave travels, that is, parallel to the direction of propagation. (अनुदैर्ध्य तरंग — कण तरंग की दिशा के समांतर कंपन करते हैं)

 

• Such waves travel as alternate regions of compression (particles crowded together, higher density and pressure) and rarefaction (particles spread apart, lower density and pressure).

 

• Sound is the most familiar example of a longitudinal wave. Longitudinal waves can travel through solids, liquids and gases, because all three resist compression.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• In a transverse wave, by contrast, the particles vibrate perpendicular to the direction of propagation, producing crests and troughs. Light and other electromagnetic waves, waves on a string and ripples on water are transverse.

 

• Transverse mechanical waves cannot travel through gases and liquids in bulk, because these do not possess rigidity (shear modulus).

 

• In an earthquake, P-waves (primary waves) are longitudinal and travel through solids as well as liquids, and are therefore the fastest and first to be recorded; S-waves (secondary waves) are transverse and cannot pass through the liquid outer core — which is how the existence of the liquid core was established.

 

• Useful formula: v = fλ, where v is the wave speed, f the frequency and λ the wavelength.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 describes a transverse wave, not a longitudinal one.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect for a plane longitudinal wave; circular or elliptical particle motion is characteristic of surface waves such as water waves and Rayleigh waves.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because wave motion is an organised, periodic vibration, not random motion — random motion of particles is thermal motion.

question: The EnVision mission, jointly supported by the European Space Agency (ESA) and NASA, is primarily intended to study which aspect of Venus?
option_2: Its surface geology and internal structure
solution_text:
The correct answer is Its surface geology and internal structure.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• EnVision is an ESA-led mission, with participation from NASA, planned as an orbiter to Venus. Its principal aim is to study the planet's surface geology, internal structure and atmosphere in order to understand why Venus and Earth, though similar in size and composition, evolved so differently. (शुक्र की सतह और आंतरिक संरचना का अध्ययन)

 

• The mission will carry radar instruments to map the surface at high resolution, a subsurface radar sounder to look beneath the crust, and spectrometers to study the atmosphere and search for signs of active volcanism and outgassing.

 

• It is planned for launch in the early 2030s and is the fifth Medium-class mission of ESA's Cosmic Vision programme.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Facts about Venus for SSC: it is the hottest planet in the solar system (surface temperature about 462°C) because of a runaway greenhouse effect caused by its dense carbon dioxide atmosphere; it is called the "Morning Star" and "Evening Star", and also the "Earth's twin" on account of its similar size and mass.

 

• Venus rotates from east to west (retrograde rotation), like Uranus, so on Venus the Sun rises in the west. Its day is longer than its year — about 243 Earth days to rotate but only about 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

 

• Other Venus missions: NASA's VERITAS and DAVINCI, and India's planned Shukrayaan-1 by ISRO. Earlier missions include the Soviet Venera series and NASA's Magellan.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect because Venus has no rings and no natural satellites (moons) — Venus and Mercury are the only planets without moons.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect; the asteroid belt lies between Mars and Jupiter, far beyond the orbit of Venus.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect because Venus has no significant intrinsic magnetic field, and in any case the mission's scope is much wider than magnetism alone.

question: Which of the following is obtained by dividing Real GDP by the total population of a country?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Per Capita Real GDP.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Per Capita Real GDP = Real GDP ÷ Total Population. It shows the average real output available per person in a country. (प्रति व्यक्ति वास्तविक सकल घरेलू उत्पाद)

 

• Real GDP is GDP measured at constant (base-year) prices, so the effect of inflation is removed. Dividing it by population therefore gives a genuine measure of the standard of living and allows comparison over time and across countries.

 

• Since it is calculated at constant prices, per capita real GDP rises only when actual production per person rises, not merely when prices rise.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Nominal GDP is measured at current prices, while Real GDP is measured at constant prices.

 

• GDP Deflator = (Nominal GDP ÷ Real GDP) × 100. It is the broadest measure of the general price level in an economy.

 

• Other national income concepts: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad; NNP = GNP − Depreciation; National Income (NNP at factor cost) = NNP at market price − Indirect taxes + Subsidies.

 

• In India, national income estimates are prepared by the National Statistical Office (NSO) under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI). The present base year for national accounts is 2011-12. The first attempt to estimate India's national income was made by Dadabhai Naoroji in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', and the first scientific estimate after independence was by the National Income Committee (1949) under P. C. Mahalanobis.

 

NOTE

 

• Nominal GDP (Option 1): The market value of all final goods and services at current prices; it is not obtained by dividing by population.

 

• GDP Deflator (Option 2): A price index, not a per-person measure.

 

• Net National Income (Option 4): Equal to GNP minus depreciation; dividing this by population would give per capita income, not per capita real GDP.

question: The Ruhr Industrial Region, famous for coal and iron industries, is situated along which river?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rhine.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ruhr Industrial Region of Germany lies in the basin of the Ruhr river, which is a tributary of the Rhine, in the state of North Rhine-Westphalia. (रूर औद्योगिक क्षेत्र — राइन नदी बेसिन)

 

• It grew into the greatest coal and iron-and-steel region of Europe because of the combination of rich coking coal deposits, cheap water transport on the Rhine, nearby iron ore, and a dense network of railways and canals.

 

• Its major industrial cities are Essen, Dortmund, Duisburg, Bochum and Düsseldorf. Duisburg on the Rhine is the largest inland port in the world.

 

• With the decline of coal mining, the region has diversified into services, technology and education, and is often cited as an example of successful industrial restructuring.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Rhine rises in the Alps of Switzerland and flows through Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, France and the Netherlands before emptying into the North Sea. It is the busiest waterway in the world in terms of inland navigation.

 

• Other major industrial regions frequently asked: the Pittsburgh region of the USA (iron and steel), the Donetsk (Donbas) basin of Ukraine, and the Chhotanagpur plateau of India.

 

NOTE

 

• Danube (Option 2): The second longest river in Europe after the Volga; it flows through ten countries, past Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Belgrade, and falls into the Black Sea.

 

• Elbe (Option 3): Rises in the Czech Republic and flows through Germany past Hamburg into the North Sea.

 

• Oder (Option 4): Forms much of the border between Germany and Poland and drains into the Baltic Sea.

question: In the context of disinvestment, what is meant by strategic disinvestment?
option_1: Sale of less than 26% stake in a public sector enterprise
option_2: Sale of government shares without transferring management
option_3: Transfer of majority ownership along with management control to a private entity
option_4: Transfer of ownership from one public sector enterprise to another
solution_text:
The correct answer is Transfer of majority ownership along with management control to a private entity.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Strategic disinvestment means the sale of a substantial portion of the government's shareholding in a Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE), of up to 50% or more, along with the transfer of management control to a strategic buyer from the private sector. (प्रबंधन नियंत्रण सहित बहुलांश हिस्सेदारी का विनिवेश)

 

• The defining feature is the transfer of management control — this is what separates strategic disinvestment from ordinary minority stake sales, where the government sells shares but continues to run the enterprise.

 

• The stated objectives are to bring in private capital, technology and managerial efficiency, to reduce the fiscal burden of loss-making enterprises, and to allow the government to concentrate on core sectors.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Disinvestment in India is handled by the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) under the Ministry of Finance. It was formerly the Department of Disinvestment and was renamed DIPAM in 2016.

 

• Methods of disinvestment: Minority stake sale, Strategic sale, Offer for Sale (OFS), Initial Public Offering (IPO), Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) such as Bharat-22 and CPSE ETF, and buyback of shares.

 

• Well-known examples of strategic disinvestment include Air India (to the Tata Group, 2021-22), and earlier cases such as VSNL, Hindustan Zinc, Modern Foods and Balco. The Disinvestment Commission was set up in 1996 under G. V. Ramakrishna.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: a sale of less than 26% is a minority stake sale, which does not affect control. A holding above 26% merely confers the power to block special resolutions.

 

• Option 2 describes exactly what strategic disinvestment is not — the essence of the strategic route is that management control does pass to the buyer.

 

• Option 4 describes a transfer between two public sector units, which leaves the enterprise within the public sector and is therefore not disinvestment in the strategic sense.

question: Which of the following books was written by Sarojini Naidu after 'The Golden Threshold'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Bird of Time.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sarojini Naidu's first published collection of poems was 'The Golden Threshold' (1905). Her next collection was 'The Bird of Time' (1912), whose full title is *The Bird of Time: Songs of Life, Death and the Spring*. (गोल्डन थ्रेशोल्ड के बाद — द बर्ड ऑफ टाइम)

 

• Her third major collection was 'The Broken Wing' (1917), which contains the well-known poem 'The Gift of India'.

 

• Sarojini Naidu is known as the "Nightingale of India" (Bharat Kokila), a title given to her by Mahatma Gandhi for the lyrical quality of her poetry.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Political achievements of Sarojini Naidu: she was the first Indian woman to become the President of the Indian National Congress (Kanpur session, 1925) — Annie Besant was the first woman President (1917) — and she became the first woman Governor of an Indian state, serving as Governor of the United Provinces (Uttar Pradesh) in 1947.

 

• She was born on 13 February 1879 in Hyderabad, and her birth anniversary is observed as National Women's Day in India. She took part in the Salt Satyagraha and led the Dharasana Satyagraha in 1930 after Gandhi's arrest.

 

NOTE

 

• The Broken Wing (Option 1): Published in 1917, that is, after 'The Bird of Time'.

 

• The Sceptred Flute (Option 3): A collected edition of her poems published in 1943, not a fresh work following 'The Golden Threshold'.

 

• The Feather of the Dawn (Option 4): A collection published posthumously in 1961, edited by her daughter Padmaja Naidu.

question: The Lomas Rishi Cave, one of the earliest examples of Indian rock-cut architecture, was dedicated to followers of which sect?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajivikas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Lomas Rishi Cave, situated in the Barabar Hills of Jehanabad district, Bihar, was dedicated to the Ajivika sect. (आजीवक संप्रदाय)

 

• It belongs to the Mauryan period (3rd century BCE) and is one of the earliest surviving examples of rock-cut architecture in India.

 

• Its most famous feature is the doorway carved in imitation of a wooden structure, with an arch-shaped (chaitya-arch) façade decorated with a row of elephants moving towards a stupa. The interior walls have the characteristic Mauryan polish, a mirror-like finish.

 

• The Ajivika sect was founded by Makkhali Gosala, a contemporary of Mahavira and the Buddha. Its central doctrine was Niyati (strict determinism or fatalism) — the belief that everything is predetermined and that human effort cannot alter destiny.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Barabar group has four caves — Lomas Rishi, Sudama, Karan Chaupar and Visvakarma. The nearby Nagarjuni Hills have three more caves, donated by Dasharatha Maurya, the grandson of Ashoka.

 

• The Sudama cave carries a dedicatory inscription of Ashoka dated to his 12th regnal year.

 

• The Barabar caves inspired the 'Marabar Caves' of E. M. Forster's novel 'A Passage to India'.

 

NOTE

 

• Buddhists (Option 1): Buddhist rock-cut architecture is seen at Ajanta, Karle, Bhaja, Bedsa, Nasik and Kanheri, but the Barabar caves were dedicated to the Ajivikas.

 

• Jains (Option 2): Jain rock-cut caves are found at Udayagiri-Khandagiri (Odisha) and Ellora (Caves 30-34).

 

• Shaivites (Option 4): Shaiva rock-cut monuments include the Kailasa temple at Ellora and the Elephanta caves, both of a much later period.

question: Which dynasty is credited with constructing the rock-cut caves at Barabar Hills?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maurya Dynasty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The rock-cut caves of the Barabar Hills in Bihar were excavated during the Mauryan period, in the 3rd century BCE, chiefly during the reigns of Ashoka and his grandson Dasharatha. (मौर्य वंश — बराबर गुफाएँ)

 

• They are the oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India and were granted to the ascetics of the Ajivika sect.

 

• Their most striking technical feature is the Mauryan polish — the interior granite walls were finished to such a smooth, glass-like sheen that they reflect light and produce a remarkable echo.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mauryan art is generally divided into court art (pillars, palaces, stupas, caves) and popular art (yaksha and yakshi figures, pottery, terracotta).

 

• Ashokan pillars are famous for their monolithic shafts and animal capitals. The Sarnath Lion Capital was adopted as the National Emblem of India on 26 January 1950, and the Dharmachakra from its abacus appears on the national flag.

 

• The Mauryan capital Pataliputra had a pillared hall resembling the Achaemenid palaces of Persepolis; Megasthenes described the city in his account 'Indica'.

 

NOTE

 

• Gupta Dynasty (Option 1): Known for structural temples such as the Dashavatara temple at Deogarh and the Bhitargaon brick temple, and for the later phases of the Ajanta paintings.

 

• Kushan Dynasty (Option 3): Associated with the Gandhara and Mathura schools of sculpture, in which the Buddha was first shown in human form.

 

• Satavahana Dynasty (Option 4): Patronised the chaityas and viharas at Karle, Bhaja, Nasik and the great toranas of Sanchi, but these belong to a period after the Mauryas.

question: Thumri is primarily associated with which of the following styles of Indian classical music?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hindustani Classical Music.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Thumri is a semi-classical vocal form of Hindustani classical music. (हिंदुस्तानी शास्त्रीय संगीत की अर्ध-शास्त्रीय गायन शैली)

 

• It is romantic and devotional in character, and its lyrics, usually in Braj Bhasha or Awadhi, most often describe the love of Radha and Krishna. Because the emotional expression of the text matters more than strict adherence to the raga, the singer is allowed considerable freedom.

 

• Thumri developed in the 19th century in the court of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Awadh (Lucknow), who was himself a poet and composer using the pen name "Akhtar Piya". Its two main styles are the Purab Ang (Banaras) and the Punjab Ang.

• Other forms of Hindustani music: Dhrupad (the oldest and most austere), Khayal (the dominant classical form), Tarana, Dhamar, Tappa, Ghazal and Qawwali.

 

• Gharanas of Hindustani vocal music: Gwalior (the oldest), Kirana, Agra, Jaipur-Atrauli, Patiala and Rampur-Sahaswan.

 

• Hindustani music is associated with North India and shows Persian and Central Asian influence, while Carnatic music belongs to South India and has remained closer to its ancient devotional roots. Amir Khusrau is credited with developing forms such as the Khayal, Tarana and Qawwali, and with the invention of the sitar and tabla by tradition.
